utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you again that this is the first time I hear of it. When you talk about the Ive Vojnovica Street, it's a very long stretch of the road. And you should be more precise as to state the exact position you're talking about in the Ive Vojnovica Street if you're insisting on me being precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that later. Do you know that in the Ive Vojnovica Street where you reside, from the artillery position of the Croatian Army, on the 6th of December 1991 170 artillery shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this. This is the first time I hear of it. And I tell you again, it was difficult for me to identify in that hell what was gunfire, what was the firing of a shell, and what was the impact of a shell and the direction it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where -- what is the location of the bridge in Ive Vojnovica Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there is not a single bridge in the Ive Vojnovica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where is the overfly in the Ive Vojnovica Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where is the crossroads where from the Ive Vojnovica Street you turn for Medarevo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know of that crossroads. There are two roads forking off, one closer to Gospino Polje heading towards the place called Gorica, near the Gorica Sveto Vlaho, and the other connects with the Ive Vojnovica Street, and I'm not sure which one of these you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, is Lazaret a protected cultural monument belonging to the A category?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this. This wasn't an area that was of interest to me, and I am not familiar with categorisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the fortress at Srdj was also a cultural monument belonging to the B category?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is the cultural protection status of the Gradac Park?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the details of the classification because this wasn't something I was closely interested in, nor did I deal with it when working with the plans. So I wouldn't even indirectly be able to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How far is Montovjerna from your house?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Montovjerna hill?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my estimate, when you go along Ive Vojnovica Street, it takes you some 8 to 10 minutes to walk there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As the crow flies, how far is the hotel complex, the camping site at Babin Kuk away from your house?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the entire peninsula?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The camping site at Babin Kuk, as the crow flies, how far is it from your house?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my estimate, a kilometre or thereabouts. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, how long have you been in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived last Saturday. My flight from Dubrovnik was delayed. And I have been in The Hague to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is this your first stay in The Hague as a witness for the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You did not come to The Hague earlier to discuss things and matters with my colleagues from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the course of this year in Dubrovnik, were you ever visited by either my colleagues here in the court or by investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did meet with the OTP investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who with and when?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, I believe, two months ago. And I'll tell you that there was Ms. Susan with two associates of hers. And the second time, there was Mr. David Re. We had a talk, and that was all we had in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long did these discussions take? First with Ms. Somers and then with the other colleagues, how long did that particular meeting last?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was sometime in the evening, and it lasted maybe for an hour, hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And with the learned colleague Re?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent some more time with him. I can't tell you precisely now. But I think we met over two days, but not for the entire day because, of course, I had my professional obligations, and I was unable to spend the entire day with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about my learned colleague tell you? What were you expected to tell to the Court?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But in addition to that, apart from telling you to tell the truth, did he tell you anything about the nature of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that I was supposed to talk about things that I professionally deal with, things that I know, and that that was the essential reason why I was invited, called to testify here. And as for the preliminary report -- and that I was supposed to testify in relation to the preliminary report made for the Old Town in Dubrovnik. And that was the intention. That's what we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In those two days of discussions with Mr. Re, which materials did you use?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown two or three videos. I'm not sure. I believe I said that at the start. They were presented to me as videos taped by Mr. Djezo Jusic. I was also shown a video by Mr. Grbic, and another video that was presented to me as the video made by the JNA. And those were the materials presented to me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you sketch any maps, you and Mr. Re, at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maps? No. I can't remember precisely. But I do know that we went through all the things that I personally signed, the plans of the Old Town, the locations I inspected. This was what actually took up most of our time. Now, whether I drew any maps I --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For instance, as today, did you make any markings on a map?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. I might have indicated the boundaries between blocks, but that could have been all that I could have done at that moment. But to tell you the truth, I can't remember really.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How much time has elapsed since this visit of Mr. Re's to Dubrovnik? It must have been this year.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I told you the extent to which I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you don't remember whether several weeks ago you and Mr. Re marked on a map individual facilities we're talking about today?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did tell you that it is quite possible that I indicated what was supposed to be presented as the block that I worked on. But it was not -- it was something that was just a summary of what I did, and I recall this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's try this again. Did you make any marks on maps with buildings several weeks ago when Mr. Re was there with you in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I've told you how far I remember. Now, how many maps, what sort of marks, I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were there several maps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- that included all the elements that were included in the report, and those were the only materials that we used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does memory serve you well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for my immediate sphere of interest, yes. For the issues of minor importance, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Marking different facilities on a map, would that constitute something -- a matter of interest to you that you would remember well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be of secondary interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, if you don't remember what and when you marked something that took place several weeks ago, how do you expect the Trial Chamber to believe you when you tell -- recount them things that happened a decade ago?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was able to work only within the information that I had on the map. On the basis of my technical expertise, I was able to talk about the whole area. Now, when you ask me about what I was able to tell the Trial Chamber, I can tell you that with high precision, I was able to retell you what I experienced in those years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have seen, Mr. Petrovic, my concern at the form of your last question. That's not for the witness to comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. I accept your criticism.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell us, prior to these discussions with my colleagues seated here in the court, did you talk to anyone else from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I may just correct my statement, when I had my first contact with the investigators, that was in 2001. And I believe you have the written statement of that. And then the other one I told you about was the second contact, and then there was the third. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of July the year 2000, did you give a written statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that was the date. I'm not sure. But if I took a look at it and I saw my signature, I would be able to testify to what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher's assistance to present this statement to the witness. It is his witness statement in English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have here is a version in Croatian which was not signed, and I have a version in English that is signed. It is my signature. I don't see what this was all about. I cannot remember that I signed the Croatian version or only the English version, but evidently on the English version I can see my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I please ask for the English version to be returned to me. Thank you. Could you please leave the statement aside now. We'll move on to that later. Tell me what this first interview looked like, the one with the investigators of the International Tribunal, in the briefest possible terms.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the briefest possible terms, I was informed by my colleagues from the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments that investigators came, that they would be willing to talk to me as one of the members of the team that worked on the preliminary report. I was informed by telephone, and I was quite simply asked whether I could come and at what time. I responded to their invitation. I came. The interview took place in the presence of a man. I don't remember his name now. He was a younger man. And the interpreter was there, too. The interpreter who spoke Croatian. And this took place in the Institute for Reconstruction. It is an institute that is involved in this kind of operational work that has to do with the reconstruction and restoration of Dubrovnik. So it was held, I mean the interview, in a meeting room. That's what I remember now. And I think it was for about two or three hours, perhaps even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, you remember that it took about two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it took about two or three hours. Its duration was two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I see. And what kind of material did you have here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on that occasion? Well, as far as I can remember, I think that I was presented with this material that we had done. So these were books, binders that in a way presented what we did in the period after the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you had before you the preliminary report, or rather what we here call P51/ID.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity of seeing this preliminary report on that occasion? Could you examine it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I scanned through it, but it was very superficial. It wasn't that I studied it carefully. Let us say I skimmed through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you look at the report in general, or did you look at the sections that you worked on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My attention was primarily focussed on what I had done. But in passing, I also looked at the sections that I did not work on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long did you take looking at your section, the one that you worked on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it didn't take very long. It was very scant information, just at first glance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you asked to look at each and every page of the report that you had worked on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that later, I was asked to confirm with my own signature the authenticity of what I had done myself. That in a way was more detailed information about what we had before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you looked at each and every page of that report that had to do with you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was all. Later on, I had established that there was a mistake, either in terms of the typing or the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please answer my question. Did you look at each and every page of the report that had to do with your inspections?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did look at them. But if that's an answer, I'll explain the rest sometime later, what I meant to tell you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign every page of the report that has to do with what you did?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed, yes, what was presented to me. And as far as I can remember, that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In addition to your signature, did you affix the date on each and every page, the 6th of July 2000?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On every page, there was the date, too, and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself put your signature and date on each and every page?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. At the moment when I signed each and every page, I put the date there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be given -- I see the exhibit already in front of him, P174.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please keep it there in front of you. So we'll be using it during our further discussion.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it this material?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Please be so kind as to look at the tenth insert, X-1. From X-1 to X-12, please look at the 11 buildings. Not the list, but within P174 itself.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the binder that is right in front of you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So X-1 to X-11.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Have you had a look at it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at it, and then tell us when you've finished. You don't have to read all the details, just --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just have a look at the exact order. Did you say to X-12 or throughout?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: To X-12.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, I've had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: X-1, X-2, X-3, and X-5, and X-6, if you look at the dates of inspection, is it the 10th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about X-7? X-9? Is the date the 11th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And X-9.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about X-10, X-11, and X-12? Is the date the 12th of December 1991, the date of inspection?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please look at your statement now, the one that is before you, the one that you gave on the 6th of July 2000. Please look at page 3 of your statement, paragraph 4 where it says: "On the 13th of December, four colleagues from the town planning office and I attended at the institute and made ourselves available to assist in the investigations which by this time were well underway." Tell us, please, when did you and your colleagues come for the first time to the office in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first contact was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did you first physically come to the institute?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around this date. But when I made this statement, in a way I think it was not additionally verified in terms of this information. After all, it was in the year 2000, almost ten years later. My memory of the date was very tentative. In a way, it was marked as the 13th. I don't know why I said the 13th. But I assumed that it was around that date more or less. I did not really insist on the actual date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did you tell the investigators and why did you sign that afterwards, that on the 13th of December 1991, you made yourself available to the institute? Why does it say the 13th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this was said with the intention of giving a time when this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, you never said "around the 13th" or you did not say "in the first half of the month," or "the second half of the month." You said specifically and precisely the 13th of December.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that point in time, this information was just an approximation of the date rather than it was supposed to be a very precise date. Had I known at the time that this precision was of such importance, I would have corrected it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the one-but-last paragraph of your statement on that same page, number 3, where it says: "Today, I signed and dated each of these investigation reports." Is it correct that before you gave this statement, or at least that's what it says here, you reviewed the report and you saw all the dates on the reports contained in it? Didn't you refresh your memory on that day, precisely on that day, in terms of what each one of the reports says? And nevertheless, did you write the date of the 13th of December stating "I made myself available for the institute"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I can say. At the moment when I signed this, I based my statement upon what I mentioned earlier; namely, that I just skimmed through the material. I did not look at each and every detail. I believed that this material which was before me actually did correspond to what I had done at the time. So this particular piece of information, namely, the date which I marked as the date when we went into town, is something that I did not consider to be essential to that statement at that moment. So it remained at that level, at the level of what I wished to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you have before you all the reports on which it says very clearly when they were made, including the 11 reports I referred to you -- I referred to a few minutes ago? Aren't they all dated before the 13th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand your question. Sorry. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you not have before you all 11 reports bearing a date that preceded the 13th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood your question, you mean these 11 that we looked at just now in this list?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you understand me well.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not look at the dates in detail because at that moment the dates were not important pieces of information to me when I was checking this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of July 2000, did you not sign each and every one of these reports, these 11 reports of the buildings that were inspected on the 10th, 11th, and 12th?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did. Everything that was offered to me and where my signature was. In a way, I initialled all of this stating in this way that it was in line with what I had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that same day did you not sign a statement including the information that you made yourself available to the institute on the 13th of December? Please give me a very precise answer to that. Was it not on that very same day that you signed a statement which says that you made yourself available to the institute on the 13th of December 1991? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have the Croatian version here with my signature and date, so I cannot tell you with any degree of certainty whether I signed all these reports on that day and the statement itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it out to you because you said a few minutes ago that on the English version, your signatures can be seen. And my colleague will follow this very carefully. What it says here: "On the 13th of December, four colleagues from the town planning office and I attended the institute and made ourselves available to assist in the investigations which by this time were well underway." Underneath is your signature and the date, the 6th of July 2000.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, then, how is it possible that on the same day you claim two different things? You put your signature on the reports dated the 10th, 11th, and 12th, and on that very same you say that you made yourself available to the institute only on the 13th. How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat to you yet again what I said. The date of the 13th at the moment when I gave the statement was an approximation of the time when we actually went out to carry out these inspections. This is the only thing I can confirm to you. And I wish we would leave this information at that level. There is really not -- nothing to add in terms of the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did you and your colleagues Buzic, Franetovic, Karaman, and Kunic, come to the institute. Did you come together?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly now whether we went individually or together. But at any rate, we had reached agreement to go to the institute. Now, in which groups we went and whether we went together or not is something I cannot remember very specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Buzic, Franetovic, Karaman, and Kunic, when did they first come to the institute?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in relation to this inspection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But, of course.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came in the same period approximately when we were supposed to start this effort; that is to say, making these tours, and that is what was mentioned here, this date in the reports or rather in the reports we made.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did they also start their work on inspecting the damage at the same time as you did?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just talk about those who worked with me. I don't know if they were parts of other teams. I cannot remember at the time. But those who were with me, they were there on the same day that I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that Ms. Karaman and Ms. Kunic began to work on the same day as you did?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were supposed to. But I don't know whether they did or not. We would need to refer back to the report because I cannot recall those details any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I will help you. Do you remember if we worked with Ms. Karaman and Ms. Kunic at all?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did work with Ms. Kunic, and I also think I worked with Mirjana Karaman. I'm not sure about her, but I know about Davorka Kunic for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please close that material in front of you, all the things that you have in front of you. Could you please just put them away. Was the inspection of the facilities in the Old Town paid?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you worked with Kunic for sure?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How many buildings did you inspect with Ms. Kunic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I would need to refer back to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you with Ms. Karaman together at the training about how your work should be done?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not go, but we got this information from our colleagues from the Institute for the Preservation of Monuments. And I was personally able to convey this information further after I received it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember after you looked at this panel and you received this information, do you remember setting out to begin your work on the same day?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having found out about what this was all about regarding this panel that you are talking about, I don't remember whether we set out on our inspections on the same day. But it was afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who did you inspect the mosque with?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, just leave the paper aside. Try to remember.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were two of my colleagues with me, but I don't know exactly who they were. I think they were probably Matko Vetma and Lucijana Peko. But I'm not a hundred per cent sure at the moment. I would have to look at the documents in order to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you look at any facility with Mr. Zeljko Franetovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you go to any inspections with Ms. Buzic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you inspect any building with Zvonimir Franic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. It was a building in which our colleagues Zvonimir Franic actually lived in. It's a block near the Domino Street and near a square. It's close to the St. Domino's church.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you inspect anything -- no, let me rephrase that. Do you know that the first time with Mrs. Kunic who came together with you, as it says in your statement, that for the first time with her, judging by that report, you went out to inspect a building together with her only on the 16th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is possible. But I'm not sure. I would need to check at that particular case to be sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Ms. Karaman, even though you said you're not sure whether you worked with her at all, joined you in the inspection of seven buildings on the 13th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would give the same answer that I gave you before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at all how these inspections were like, what they were like?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it strange to you that none of your associates did not inspect or participate in the inspection of any facilities before the 13th?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that that is unusual in any way. The inspections were completed with colleagues when they were able to come. Coming to the old Dubrovnik centre was something gradual. Our teams were completed gradually so that the teams from the urban town planning institute joined this work incrementally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, is it strange that none of your colleagues about whom, at least according to your statement, you said they came together with you, that none of them inspected any facilities before the 13th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, none of these things should be taken literally. It's more of a figurative nature, and it describes an activity which simply indicates a process that took a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to come back to a sentence from your statement on page 3, paragraph 4, where you clearly state in describing your activities during one day, that is, on the 13th of December, and you say: "On the 13th, four colleagues and myself attended the institute and made ourselves available." There are no activities there lasting over weeks or months. This is about your activities on the 13th of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the date can be given an interpretation, like I said before. It's an approximate date. Secondly, making ourselves available for assistance is a lasting activity. It's not something that ended at that time. So if we're actually going for precision, we cannot just take it the way you explained it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please then explain to us "to be available for assistance in the investigations which by this were well underway"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to go word for word or do you just want me to provide an explanation of the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, arrival on the 13th and making yourselves available for the investigations which by this time were well underway?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This phrasing can just be defined provisionally in the sense of describing what was happening in that period. The time is approximate. The activities are approximate, the activities we were supposed to carry out and which we did carry out. And thirdly, it describes in relation to these activities of ours something that had already been started. When it says here "were well underway," it means that this was already being carried out before the 6th of December as well as after the 6th of December. So that the way this is phrased does not indicate the quantity of information, but it just indicates that the process had begun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that when you say "well underway," you are thinking of activities before the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I am predominantly thinking of activities after the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many buildings were inspected in the period before the 13th?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Approximately?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not make any kind of statistical report so I really wouldn't be able to give you any approximate number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have another break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, before December 1991, did you have any experience relating to determining the manner, the time, the cause, and the effects of damages on a building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My main qualifications were actually based on identifying the present state of the cultural heritage, and this is something that we were trained for during our university education. We had exercises and learned about how to identify certain conditions of cultural and historical monuments. I worked professionally on a building complex, the music school building complex in Dubrovnik, and I did an architectural inspection of that building, determined its current state, drafted also how this building was going to be restored, and presented what the building was going to look like after the reconstruction. This was simply part of our basic training.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Besides the elementary training, do you have any other experience in determining damage on a building caused by a fire, for example?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Experiences on monuments belonging to the cultural heritage is -- consists actually of what I spoke earlier. You needed to determine what the cause was of the damage, the extent of the damage, and those experiences were actually something that was implied through our elementary training. On the other hand, when we're talking about incidents like this of such a scale, when we're talking about earthquakes based on additional expert information, you could even train somebody in a very short period of time who did not have our education in order to be able to determine the existing state of a certain building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific in answering my question. My question is: Do you have any experience in determining the cause of a fire on a building prior to the 6th of December? Did you have such experiences prior to the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not regarding the cause of a fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever determine the cause of fire on any kind of building before the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever determine the cause of damage due to weapons or ammunition?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not prior to that. And by that I mean, not prior to the 6th of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you know anything about the types, the models of projectiles, except for what you read on the panel at the institute when you got there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any detailed information about that, other than what I saw at the panel for the preservation of cultural monuments. I can also add to that the knowledge that I had acquired during my military service in the JNA which I served in Banja Luka from 1980 to 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you have a permanent team in order to inspect these buildings featured in Exhibit P174?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These situations could not have been foreseen, so we did not have the possibility of forming permanent teams. Especially not prior to these incidents. This is an ad hoc situation which quite understandably called for quite a different kind of organisation. So the way in which we proceeded was also the result of such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did the people constantly change, those people who conducted these inspections with you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean with me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, with you personally.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depended on the availability of certain person people who could assist at a particular time. That was the only reason, no other reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever before make inspection reports on the damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking of the type of damage which we saw in the period after the 6th, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you succeed in personally touring each of these buildings mentioned in P174?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally inspected each building that I said I had inspected and signed that I had inspected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did each member of the team inspect each of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking of the team that I worked in, then all the buildings were inspected by the whole team, the same way that I inspected the buildings, the other members inspected them, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How much time did you have for each building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the degree of damage. When we had minor damage, we needed less time, and when we had major damage, we needed more time. But on average, it was from 20 minutes to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What needed to be done in that 20-minute to half-an-hour period?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of our inspection, the primary thing that we did was acquire visual information, what we were able to see when we came into the building, if there were any traces of damage. The second part was talking to the inhabitants of a building or to the people who lived in neighbouring buildings, perhaps across from the building that we were inspecting or people who lived in buildings in the block next to the building we were inspecting. So that was the basic concept of how we approached our inspections. And based on the information that we had, prior expert information that we had before as to what could be the cause of impact and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you write that down when you were there out on the location?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you make a kind of sketch when you were out in the field?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We noted the building that we worked on on the map, and we also took notes by hand, and we filled in the information that was required in the questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you did not sketch any of the damaged buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you photograph the damaged buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I personally did not. But there were photographers from the Institute for the Preservation of Cultural Monuments. They made photographs. However, they did not take pictures of each building due to the technical nature of our work. It was not possible to photograph each building. Some spaces were very tight, and there were also limitations as regards developing the film. We didn't have water. We didn't have electricity. So this was an activity that had to be reduced to a minimum.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you did not photograph each building because some buildings, because of their position it was not possible to photograph. That's the first reason. And the second reason is that you didn't have water or electricity in order to be able to develop the film.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this other reason was secondary, but the main reason was also because there weren't enough people. This was done by just one man, and he was not able to be in every building that was being inspected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, my learned colleague showed you the front page of the report where it says that there were four or five photographers who did the job, if I am not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think you misread that. There were two photographers, one of them was a professional working for the Institute for the Protection --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the name.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the second was Djukic who was a photographer working there, and those are the two that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind and look at the binder in front of you and tell us which facility could not be photographed due to the facility's position and why, why couldn't it be photographed.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you that the photographs were attached here on the basis of the material that my colleague collected from the Institute for the Preservation of Cultural Monuments. He would go out on his initiative on the basis of what he knew of the shelled site, and his attention was focussed at the time on the vital institutions, that is, the monastery, churches, palaces, and bell towers, and possibly also the ramparts. And in addition to the information that we would provide to him --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This was not my question. My question was, which facility could not be photographed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those facilities for which the photographs have not been appended here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, this means that those facilities could not be photographed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, not at that moment, they could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: These handwritten notes, what did you do with them later on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We organised them and made a paper out of them. I don't remember how it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You finished your work in the field. What did you do in physical terms with the notes you made?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We placed it on a desk, and then each and every copy, handwritten copy, was transformed into an expedited [as interpreted] version which could be forwarded on for typing out and for being organised in terms of its layout.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is contained in the exhibit P174 is that what you personally typed out or did you dictate it to someone?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither of these. We provided them with a manuscript of handwritten material that was then copied, typed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that transcript later on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it when it was a finished product. It was already sort of a binder that contained several volumes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you double check whether your notes matched the text that was typed out?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did that, but not letter by letter, number by number. And there might have been some typographical mistakes, errors, there. But if you took any extract here at random, it did match our handwritten notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did you not place your signature on these notes at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we were asked to do that at the time. And I don't think that it affects the credibility of the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, or the day before, you told us that you did write the date of damage for most of the buildings. Are there any buildings that you didn't write the date of when the damage was incurred?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We personally wrote the date for each and every building, but possibly while the materials were being transcribed, some of the data might have been left out. I could not intervene. But even if this was the case, it was very sporadic, maybe in one or two cases it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In cases when there were no tenants in the building, who did you obtain information from?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And when there were no neighbours available, what did you do in that case?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must say that we were lucky in having either tenants or neighbours present because it was done at the time when people were returning home. They were trying to make these places habitable so that in cases when there were no tenants there would at least be neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how did you manage to be present at two places at the same time while you were making these lists?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you sometimes manage to be at three places at the same time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean during one day, then my answer is yes. But at the same time, then no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I will read this out to you. On the 16th of December at 11.00, you were inspecting the facility XI-16. At 11.00, at the same time, you were inspecting the facility XI-17.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me what you're talking about in order for me to follow visually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Of course. XI-16, XI-17, you were visiting these two facilities at 11.00, and also the facility XI-19. How did you manage to inspect three facilities at 11.00?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said XI-16?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: XI-17 and XI-19. You were allegedly present at all these three facilities at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said 16, 17, and?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been a typographical error. This was supposed to be an approximate piece of information for us. But this must have been mistyped.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How do you know it's an error when you did not match if they tallied your notes?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because something like that would never have been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It would never have been done, provided that you were there at 11.00 at all these three facilities?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But since probably you were present only at some facilities and not at others, then it states here that you were at three different places at the same time.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's the day that matters. And as for the time, there must have been an error. I can confirm that this is the exclusive reason for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th of December, you were also present at three places at the same time, facilities XI-23, XI-26, XI-27. At all of these three facilities, you were present at the same time, at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: 17 December, the facilities 23, 26, 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How did you manage in this case to be present at the same time at three different places?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said XI-23, XI-26. Which was the other one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: XI-23, XI-26, and XI-27.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a situation similar to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you were --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there, and this must have been a typographical error, mistyping what we had written in the manuscript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How did you manage on that same day, on the 17th of December, at 10.10 hours to be at the facility XI-24 and at the same time visiting the facility XI-25?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the same reasons as previously can be applied here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So there's an error at hand again?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How can we verify that that is what indeed happened? There are no photographs. There are no sketches. We don't have your working notes. We only have this piece of information that you were at three different places at the same time.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be confirmed by indicating what had been done -- what had already been done on that facility when it was undergoing reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how did you manage in ten minutes to inspect five facilities, XI-23, 24, 25, 26, 27? All of them having been processed between 10.00 and 10.10?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This must be an error again. But it's the same situation that you could put to your members of the team who have apparently, according to their notes, managed to inspect the JNA, has managed to inspect the entire town in two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So it must have been a similar situation.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Here we have several facilities inspected over several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How did you manage on the 16th of December to be at two places at the same time, facilities XI-30 and XI-31? You visited those at 1400 hours. How did you manage again to be at two different places at the same time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My previous answer is valid again. We relied on the date to denote the day when they were there. The time wasn't as important. So that's one thing. So even if there was an error, it does not substantially affect our work done on that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is the accuracy of what you've written down given all these errors?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is accurate given that an assessment was made on the basis of this material in determining what the damage was. And on the other side, there were other projects that were developed that were supposed to be the basis for the reconstruction of these facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was the situation like on the 17th of December, facilities XI-32, XI-33? Again, you were at these two facilities at the same time on the 17th of December.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be the same error again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The same error.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, the technical, typographical error.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How was it possible for you on the 15th of December, these were facilities XI-22 and XI-23, to be at both these facilities at the same time, at 13.30?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And XI-23. You were present at both these facilities at the same time, at the same moment. What was the situation like here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same situation. If there indeed exists such a proximity of time as this, then it merely means that these two facilities were close to each other. So that's why we used this time. We basically looked at these two facilities at the same time or even at other facilities because we were able to view these different facilities at the same time either when looking from it from the street or from other angles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of December --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... I think there's an error in the last one. The two I have, XI-22 and XI-23 seem to say different times. XI-23 says 1000 hours, and XI-22 says 10 -- sorry, it says 9.45. Maybe my learned friend meant to refer to different buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I made a mistake, and I apologise to everyone, first of all to you. It was IX-22 and IX-23. Reports IX-22 and IX-23.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You were present at both these facilities, IX-22 and IX-23 at 10.00, both these buildings. Was there an error here as well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was an error again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The buildings X-2 and X-3, was there an error as well because you seem to have been at these two buildings at 1200 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which ones did you mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: X-2 and X-3. There you were at these two different places at the same time.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These buildings are in immediate vicinity of one another. This other building at Buniceva Poljana was on our way to this other building that we looked at in greater detail. So that's why we identified them at the same time. I do remember that there were such cases as this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So these were mostly mistakes?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as I've said, this piece of information for us had secondary value. We didn't attach much importance to it. We thought the date was much more important than the time of inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Fine. If the date is more important, please tell me the following: We are talking about the 17th of December. 18 locations, 23 buildings were inspected by you between 9.45 and 13.20. How were you able to inspect 23 buildings in a bit over three hours?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was possible because not all the buildings were damaged to the same extent. And we would spend different intervals of time at different buildings. I've told you from some 20 minutes to half an hour, 45 minutes. That's why it was impossible [as interpreted] within this three-hour interval.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That day when you visited 23 buildings --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may just digress a bit, which buildings are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the date of 17th December.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell me what the block was. That's easier for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These a blocks 11 -- I mean, primarily block 11.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I can read out the number if you think that my records aren't adequate enough.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean then the entire block 11 that I worked on? Yes, that's next to Od Puca Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, my question.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How did you manage in 9 minutes and 20 seconds for each of these 23 buildings, how did you manage to inspect their damage, to talk with the neighbours, to write down the date of impact, the type and number of projectile, to number the damages, the holes, storeys? How did you manage to do that for all the 23 buildings in 9 minutes and 27 seconds for each? Who can do such a thing?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please have some more time to concentrate, and then I'll give you the answer. I'll give you a response in relation to what I said a few minutes ago. During these inspections, there were some buildings where the situation was more than evident, those that were burned down completely. There was no need to stop and spend any time there. They could have been dealt with very briefly, those that were completely destroyed. So basically, we would stay at such buildings only for us to see for ourselves what had happened, and that would be very brief indeed. As for the other buildings that you refer to here, the brevity of time referred to and the description here are things that you have to take into consideration, and I kindly ask the Honourable Trial Chamber to bear this many mind. Quite simply, if we did not have sufficient information during our first inspection, we would go for additional inspections, and then we would take more notes and in this way supplement our reports. So what you refer to now is a description that is disproportionate to the time spent there, so it's only a relevant truth. We inspected the buildings yet again. We went there yet again, but this was not recorded anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why is it only now after three or four days of examination that you tell us now for the very first time that you went for these additional inspections? How come this is not contained in your statement? It is not contained in your examination-in-chief. How come you remember only now?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this examination has gone on for quite a while, and I believe that the level of information that I am now trying to remember is stimulative enough in order to help me remember all these additional pieces of information, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that probably has to be an addition to your testimony when you say that when you returned from these inspections, you would present your reports at a desk, and then they would be further processed. So you wish to correct your statement in that respect, too?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. In that part, and I don't think that this would diminish the importance of what's being said in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So what are you correcting in respect of what you said now?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you put your report on the table, you said a few minutes ago that you would return from your inspection and you would put the report on the desk. So what do you correct now?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That our job ended there and then. This is actually a continuous verb. It went on and on, our job did. So we had to give additional pieces of information. We had to go back for further inspections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you do this and when?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly. But for example, these examples that you pointed out now, it is possible that they were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is this contained anywhere in the report that additional inspections were carried out?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it referred to anywhere that additional inspections were carried out?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I know, no. At least not where I personally worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How can we believe you? It's not contained in the report; it's not contained in your notes; there's nothing. There is your statement which changed twice over the past 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement has only been supplemented, but the essence has remained the same. The fact is that inspections were carried out on that day, the day that is mentioned. As for the rest, I believe that this is only additional information that can practically be interpreted in one way or the other. But this basically does not diminish the importance of what was written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell us why you changed your statement with regard to yet another matter, not exactly 15 minutes ago but, say, 20 minutes ago. In response to my question "where did you spend most of your time, where did you stay the longest," you said "where the damage was the greatest, the most serious, the biggest." That's what you told us about 20 minutes ago. Then about 5 minutes ago, you said to us that where the damage was the greatest, you practically did not spend any time there, so are you changing your statement yet again?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the statement was of a general nature, and I think this means that as far as greater damage is concerned, when more time was needed to establish it, especially the second and third category, then -- so I'm speaking in principle, I'm speaking in general. More time was required. And it was even necessary to go back to collect additional information, as I said a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And that's not different from what you said a short while ago?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that, where the damage was big, you spent a lot of time there. That's what you said 20 minutes ago, and that's what you said now. And 5 minutes ago you said when the damage was big, you did not really spend any time there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It only had to do with the buildings that burned down and they are an exception. And I think I actually said to in one of my previous statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How many such buildings were involved, or rather on this day, when you inspected -- the 17th of December, when you inspected 23 buildings and you spent 9 minutes and 20 seconds inspecting each and every one of them on average, how many of them were totally burned down?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About four were totally burned down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My objection is simply it's Mr. Petrovic's dividing time by buildings and saying it took 9 minutes and 23 seconds or whatever, that's not the witness's evidence. And the witness has already answered that it took much less if a building was completely burnt out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An integral part of the evidence that is being introduced through this evidence witness before the Honourable Trial Chamber is this document, this document is the basis. He read out from this document all the time about the damage that he registered. He has only been testifying on the basis of this document, with the exception of the buildings that you asked him about, Your Honour, whether he remembered them independently of this. So the only thing I have before me is this report. And in that report, it says that he inspected 23 buildings in 3 hours and 20 minutes. That's what I asked him about. I don't see what it is that my learned friend is challenging.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the difference between you is over the words "on average," which you put in at the end of the question, if I remember it. The witness has indicated he took different times with different buildings, and your question, at least initially, created the impression that you were saying that his evidence was that he took 9 minutes and 20 seconds or thereabouts for each building. But you then added "on average," which technical means you're in the clear, but there remains force in Mr. Re's objection. I think you can be confident, Mr. Petrovic, that the points you're making have been well and truly appreciated by the Chamber, and I'd suggest you move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could the witness please have P172 placed before him, if it's not already there. Perhaps it is already before the witness, but I can't see from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, the day before yesterday on page 18 of the transcript, that is to say, the LiveNote, the unofficial transcript, you said that on the 7th of December when you came to the Old Town, you went towards your mother's house. And then you said: "I saw something that shocked me because it had to do with my mother's life. Usually she was on the ground floor. On that occasion, she was one storey above. When the shell fell, it completely destroyed the very solid door of his house." Then my learned friend asked you "what else did you see?" And you said: "I saw there in front of my mother's house on the facade some traces." And my learned friend said "what kind of traces on the facade?" And you say: "Traces on the stone facade." And you're referring to your mother's house all the time. Could you please be so kind as to find on this map, rather, within P172, the building where your mother lived. And then I'm going to put further questions to you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is block 10. Block 10, but it wasn't specially indicated. This block that you're talking about, if I may just add to this information --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. Allow me. Is there on the map, P172, on this list of ten buildings, is one of those buildings the building that I hope your mother still lives in? Could you please put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the building, and this is the door that we talked about. The shell was here. So this is where the shell struck and broke through the door. It riddled the door --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, do not make any markings on the document which was introduced by my colleague for other purposes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I just wanted to show you what I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the preliminary report, could you please tell us where --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could that document he just marked which has a 10 on it perhaps be separated from that and a photocopied one be substituted so we know what he has marked on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not sure why you want that done, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Because the exhibit P172 is an aide memoire to the Chambers, and -- the Trial Chamber, and the witness has just marked in a sense in a way that it is not evidence of something that happened to his mother's house and is a representation of where a shell or whatever landed. And that in my submission should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want this page marked as a separate exhibit. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please, extracted. And a substitute page 10 put in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I can we can pursue that, but I think we'll see whether there is a motion to admit it as evidence later. We will allow the substitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, you inspected all the facilities in Buniceva Poljana where your mother lives, and these are buildings marked with 1, 2, 3, 4. These buildings are all at Buniceva Poljana. Could you please kindly tell me where in your reports does it state that there is such a shocking damage that you noticed on the 7th of December when you came into Old Town for the first time afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will answer you. I do not see first of all that 4 is on Buniceva Poljana. It's on Gunduliceva Poljana. And it's a fountain. Buniceva Poljana is this location here. Number 4 refers to something else, and that is Gunduliceva Poljana, and the fountain is number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's make this short. Within the zone which was the subject of your inspection, where is the most shocking scene that you encountered which could have an effect on the life on a person who is most dear to you? Where is that stated in the report that you developed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My description of it being shocking is of a highly personal nature because it has something to do with the life of my mother. The shocking part does not refer to the extent of the damage, but what I was shocked about is the fact that all the time during the shelling she was in the -- she was on the ground floor. And that day, she was not just incidentally on the ground floor. Had she been there, she would have been killed in the shelling. So that was what was shocking to me. As far as the physical damage is concerned, I said in my previous testimony that the apartment in which my mother lived at the time and in which she still lives was not damaged to such an extent that it should be registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So the door was damaged, the stone facade was damaged by shrapnel from a mine which allegedly exploded in front of it within your zone. So this is not relevant enough to be recorded in the report that we are discussing?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were similar examples which only confirms that what we were doing indicates that the number of damaged buildings was not exaggerated, but that there were probably more than we mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The reason why you were not sure why you spent a part of your life together with your mother in Buniceva Poljana number 4 or number 6. And I will tell you the reason why you were not sure. The house you say is Buniceva Poljana number 4 is actually marked here as Buniceva Poljana number 3. The second reason is that the description of the damage at Buniceva Poljana number 4 has nothing to do with the damage that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is in reference to Document X-3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read a little more slowly what you said in the beginning because I think that some of the claims you are making are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I suggest that we continue this conversation tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it would be useful if you would just read once more, more slowly. That will allow the witness to think overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The reason why you could not recall whether your mother lives at Buniceva Poljana number 4 or Buniceva Poljana number 6 is in the fact that the description of the damage that exists for Buniceva Poljana number 4 is completely different from what you have described for this Trial Chamber. Could you please look at document X-3 and tell us whether the damage there corresponds to what you described to the Trial Chamber as having shocked you on the 7th of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building of Buniceva Poljana number 4 about which you are stating that I am unsure about when we're talking about the number of the house that my mother lives in, that was not my intention. In my statement, I did not wish to create any confusion. It is just a result of total lack of information. It's just a question of shadings in what we are describing. The damage on my mother's house were not reported as relevant in these reports because, as I said before, there were many such examples, and we did not consider each one to be important enough to record as damaged buildings. When we're talking about Buniceva Poljana number 4, that is the building in front of which a shell fell. And this is drawn here very clearly, and also described. So I don't know what is disputed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the end of this questioning, at least, are you sure that your mother lives in number 4 or whether she lives in number 6, or still not sure about that? This is my last question today.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She lives in this building that I have shown here. She lives here. I don't know what number that is. I'm still not sure. But if in our description we marked this as number 4, then it's possible that this is number 6, or some other number. But the number referred to as number 3 for this house, that for certain has that house number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will -- yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, could the witness possibly mark with an X on that T-shaped building he said was his mother's house before we leave so that it doesn't get lost - it just won't show up on the transcript - and it be extracted from there, marked for identification, and I can give the Registry an identical copy of page 10 to put back in just so we don't lose what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please kind enough, Mr. Vukovic, on that page 10 of the exhibit that's in front of you to mark with a large X the residence of your mother.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now adjourn until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 7th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
